originalTitle: Adam Mosseri says negativity around AI is ‘going to get worse’
summary: Asked about AI and the trend of college students booing tech CEOs at graduation ceremonies, Instagram head Adam Mosseri acknowledged in an interview that a lot of people really don't like AI, and it's not just young people and creatives. content: Asked about AI and the trend of college students booing tech CEOs at graduation ceremonies, Instagram head Adam Mosseri acknowledged in an interview that a lot of people really don’t like AI, and it’s not just young people and creatives. Appearing on the Colin and Samir podcast to talk about the launch of widescreen and long-form video for Instagram, Mosseri said he thinks there’s a trend of “more anxiety and more frustration and more anger about AI,” particularly in creative industries: > It’s not only getting worse, it’s going to continue to get worse. I think we’re going to see more frustration and anger, some of it founded, some of it unfounded, over the next couple of years, and that’s going to make it hard for a lot of people, not just in the industry. [Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sxizdQ2hRfk&t=3689s] Mosseri claimed Instagram doesn’t rank AI creators differently, but raised the question of ranking quality, saying, “There’s a lot of great AI content out there, there’s also a lot of AI slop. Do we rank AI content as well as we rank non-AI content? Probably not.” Talking about AI slop again after previously bringing it up in a New Year’s slideshow dump, he said he thinks the term AI “slop” is used “too liberally.” Instagram began cracking down on AI-generated profiles in August, after launching a label for AI accounts earlier this year, but misleading AI content like celebrity deepfakes remains an issue. Earlier this month, Mosseri said Instagram is “actively working out what to do” about AI fakes, but he noted, “I don’t think it’s practical for us to try and ban AI content from the platform.” Mosseri said Instagram is “now starting to require AI accounts to label themselves, because we think it’s important that people know if what they’re looking at is real or not real.” He also acknowledged there are fears around AI, including from creators: > I think people are concerned about a lot of things. I think they’re concerned about owning their content and models getting trained on their content. I think they’re concerned— there’s people who are concerned about safety. They’re concerned about job displacement, having AI displace whatever it is they do, if you’re a content creator or an engineer or a mathematician. I think there’s concerns about— I mean, fundamentally what I think it comes down to when you really have, like, a heart-to-heart with someone is a fear of being left behind in some way.
chineseTitle: Adam Mosseri 表示，围绕 AI 的负面情绪“将会变得更糟”
chineseSummary: 当被问及人工智能和大学生在毕业典礼上嘘科技首席执行官的趋势时，Instagram 负责人 Adam Mosseri 在接受采访时承认，很多人确实不喜欢人工智能，而且不仅仅是年轻人和创意人士。出现在科林和萨米尔播客上谈论宽屏和 [...]
chineseContent: 当被问及人工智能和大学生在毕业典礼上嘘科技首席执行官的趋势时，Instagram 负责人 Adam Mosseri 在接受采访时承认，很多人确实不喜欢人工智能，而且不仅仅是年轻人和创意人士。 Mosseri 在 Colin 和 Samir 播客中谈论 Instagram 宽屏和长视频的推出时表示，他认为存在一种“对人工智能更加焦虑、沮丧和愤怒”​​的趋势，特别是在创意行业： > 情况不仅变得更糟，而且还会继续变得更糟。我认为，在接下来的几年里，我们将看到更多的沮丧和愤怒，有些是有根据的，有些是毫无根据的，这会让很多人感到困难，而不仅仅是行业内的人。 [媒体：https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sxizdQ2hRfk&t=3689s] Mosseri 声称 Instagram 不会以不同的方式对人工智能创作者进行排名，但提出了排名质量的问题，他说：“那里有很多很棒的人工智能内容，但也有很多人工智能废话。我们对人工智能内容的排名是否和对非人工智能内容的排名一样？可能不会。”继之前在新年幻灯片转储中提到人工智能“slop”之后，他再次谈到人工智能“slop”，他表示，他认为“人工智能”“slop”这个词的使用“过于随意”。 Instagram 在今年早些时候推出了人工智能账户标签后，于今年 8 月开始打击人工智能生成的个人资料，但名人深度假货等误导性人工智能内容仍然是一个问题。本月早些时候，Mosseri 表示 Instagram 正在“积极研究如何应对”人工智能造假问题，但他指出，“我认为我们尝试禁止该平台上的人工智能内容并不实际。” Mosseri 表示，Instagram“现在开始要求人工智能账户给自己贴上标签，因为我们认为人们知道他们正在看的内容是否是真实的，这一点很重要”
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于 AI 与科技趋势信号，适合用于观察工具选型、产品机会、开发者关注点和技术路线变化。
